An R package for analyzing agricultural experiment data in the Thai context. It turns raw data into ready-to-use statistical reports, like freshly cooked rice (ข้าวสวย) ready to serve.

[Package documentation](https://kanthjs.github.io/khaosuay/){.btn-link-out target="_blank"} [GitHub](https://github.com/kanthjs/khaosuay){.btn-link-out target="_blank"}

## Why khaosuay?

Statistical analysis of field experiments (CRD, RCBD, split-plot) involves a lot of fiddly work: preparing data, checking assumptions, and drawing publication-ready charts. khaosuay wraps this into a short pipeline, supports Thai column names, and chooses between parametric and non-parametric tests automatically.

## The four-step workflow

| Step | Function | Metaphor | What it does |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `wash_rice()` | Wash the rice | Clean data, detect outliers, check the design |
| 2 | `taste_rice()` | Taste the rice | Check normality and equal variance |
| 3 | `cook_crd()` / `cook_rcbd()` / `cook_split()` | Cook the rice | Run the analysis for the experimental design |
| 4 | `plot_cooked()` | Serve the rice | Plot results with significance letters |

## Install

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("kanthjs/khaosuay")
```
